I'm in sort of a strange situation. I'm still at a point where I can progress linearly, yet I've decided to go on a cut for the next couple of months to get rid of some excess fat that's been bugging me. I find that cutting most seriously impacts my ability to recover between workouts. Since I've always heard you're no longer a beginner when you can't recover between workouts, does this mean I should switch to a more advanced program temporarily?

Currently I'm just continuing to give max effort MWF, but progress is very slow and I'm getting my ass kicked.

TL;DR What should a beginner who is running a linear program do on a cut?
Switch to an intermediate program when cutting?

In my opinion you should run the linear program as long as you can and do a cut after the linear progress stops and then do something like 5/3/1 while on a moderate cut, if you decide to cut before you've added the base strength and muscle that comes along with beginner programs then you'll most likely just look really skinny.

Do linear progression for probably another month then switch to intermediate and start cutting.
Thanks! I was running linear for about six weeks, so I'll have to see how it looks. If I start looking too skinny I'll just start eating again and bulk up.
Oh in that case running a linear for another 4 weeks is what you should do considering you should lose about 4lbs in that time frame and can shorten the whole progress thing.

Keep on what you're doing, and let your efforts tell you when to switch. If you can maintain linear progression on a cut, then you are leaving 'gainz' at the gym by switching too soon. If the recovery is too brief, you'll see the effects in your training and a switch would be in order.

Also remember: no one can stop you from customizing your training plan. If you consistantly plateau in one lift and still progress in another, you can deload and introduce more advanced training techniques specific to the stalling lift while maintaining a linear progression on the second lift. For example, if you are running a full-body routine with an A/B split and your squat is repeatedly stalling while your bench-press is progresses, you can take a cue from Westside and introduce speed work at a lighter weight for your squat on alternating days. Other examples could be variations (eg. front squats) on alternating sessions, across the board reduction of volume for that lift (eg. 5x5 -> 5x3 always for that lift), or even just reducing or dropping the exercise on alternating sessions. You sound like you have an idea of where you want to take your training next, so you can identify some training features of the next program and make the transition from your current routine less abrupt. Food for thought.
You can lose fat while building muscle man, especially as a beginner. Just cut your calories back a slight bit.
